grand_strategy.reading:
Malaysia is the middle power that chairs the room and sells neutrality in it. Its currency is access, not force: Xi in April 2025 and Trump in October, Hamas's political wing and Washington's trade negotiators, BRICS partner status and the Five Power Defence Arrangements, all at once. In Luttwak's terms its strength is that the other powers cannot settle the room without it, and its weakness is that the neutrality has to be re-earned each time a power presses. The 2025 chair is the clearest case: the Putrajaya ceasefire and the Kuala Lumpur accord gave Kuala Lumpur a stage, then Thailand's suspension and the December fighting showed that the stage rested on Trump's attention; the reciprocal trade deal repeated the pattern in 2026, signed in October, voided in March, yet still setting the tariff. At home the logic runs the other way: the Malay vote that rewards Gaza and neutrality is the one UMNO, PAS and Najib's pardon now contest, and the election is due within 16 months.
Signals that are not rows: Anwar in Shanghai in September 2026 saying that Malaysia stays neutral and that Beijing understood; UMNO's dare of the same month; the rail extension to the Thai border agreed in principle and not yet approved. Gaps in this pass (no source read, nothing written): Japan, Turkey (drones, the Islamic axis), Saudi Arabia and the Gulf (hajj, petrochemicals), Iran (ship-to-ship transfers), and the detail of Australia, the UK and New Zealand beyond the FPDA; Singapore's water price and Pedra Branca rest on one tier-4 pointer.

stances.note: Partner, not reluctant partner: Kuala Lumpur does not resist China, it declines to align with it (Anwar, September 2026: Malaysia stays neutral under US pressure and Beijing understood). China has been the largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years (US$132.5bn in 2025, 17.7% of trade) and, level with Singapore, the largest source of approved FDI (MYR58.0bn of a record MYR426.7bn in 2025); Xi's state visit of 15-17 Apr 2025 produced 45 documents and Anwar's Shanghai and Hangzhou trip of September 2026 MYR28.6bn of potential investment and an in-principle extension of the East Coast Rail Link to the Thai border (not yet approved). The friction is kept quiet: Chinese coast guard vessels sit beside Kasawari and the Luconia Shoals and Petronas keeps drilling. Warming on the evidence of 2025-26. Bond affinity is our reading (Anwar called Xi an 'outstanding leader' in June 2024; a large ethnic Chinese minority); no source calls it kinship.

Partner in the sense that matters: the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (MOU 11 Jan 2024, agreement signed in January 2025, welcomed at the 12th leaders' retreat on 4 Dec 2025; S$5.5bn of Singapore-based commitments since January 2024), the RTS Link, both are FPDA members, and Singapore stands level with China as the top FDI source in 2025. Bond grievance rather than kin, as on the Singapore side: the separation of 1965 and the disputes it left, our reading; the family ties are real but have never ended a dispute. ASEAN neighbour and partner in everyday terms (Manila took over the 2026 chair from Kuala Lumpur at the 47th summit, October 2025), with an old wound underneath: the Sabah claim that the Philippines has never formally dropped. Partner because neither state wants the claim to move; bond grievance because it is open. Confidence C: no 2025-26 government statement found.

stances.note: Argued: rival, not adversary. The ontology reserves 'adversary' for a declared aim of the other's defeat or disappearance; Kuala Lumpur does not seek Israel's end - Communications Minister Fahmi said in December 2023 that the port ban signals that Malaysia does not recognise Israel, the government advocates a two-state solution and says it will establish relations only after a peace agreement with the State of Palestine. But it is far more than neutral: Israel has never been recognised and there are no relations; ZIM and Israeli-flagged ships have been barred and Israel-bound cargo cannot be loaded since December 2023 (no sign it was lifted; not re-verified for 2026); Anwar called the Gaza strikes 'the height of barbarism' (Oct 2023), met Hamas leaders in Doha (May 2024) and mourned Sinwar (Oct 2024), and Wisma Putra called the interception of the Global Sumud Flotilla on 2 Oct 2025 'criminal and cowardly acts of aggression'. No source uses the word 'rival': the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C). Bond grievance: Palestine as a standing cause in Malay-Muslim politics.

relations_to.summary: Limbang: Brunei's claim to the Limbang district of Sarawak, dormant since the 2009 exchange of letters. Malaysian press reported in March 2009 that Brunei had dropped it; Brunei denied this, saying the Limbang question was never discussed in the exchange of letters. Dormant, not withdrawn.

relations_to.summary: The Philippines has never formally renounced its historic claim to Sabah, but it is dormant at state level; the live case is the private claim of Sulu heirs (a USD 14.9bn arbitral award of 2022 against Malaysia, which rejects it) and Anwar said in 2023 he had no evidence of Philippine government involvement. No government statement of 2025-26 found.

sources.title: The Philippines' Sabah claim: Legacy, law and likely outcome

relations_to.summary: The Five Power Defence Arrangements (1971) tie Singapore and Malaysia, with Australia, New Zealand and the UK, in consultation on their external defence; the defence ministers met on 31 May 2025 at the Shangri-La Dialogue and expected the UK Carrier Strike Group to join Exercise Bersama Lima 2025. A consultative arrangement, not a mutual-defence treaty.

relations_to.summary: The Johor River Water Agreement of 29 Sep 1962 (99 years, to 2061, up to 250 million gallons a day) and the 1990 agreement that allowed the Linggiu dam, also to 2061, are the legal basis of Singapore's imported water; at the December 2025 leaders' retreat both sides reaffirmed the 1962 agreement and left price, yield and quality to a Joint Technical Committee.

relations_to.summary: In 2025 piped gas from Malaysia and Indonesia was 43% of Singapore's gas imports and LNG 57% (Energy Market Authority); more than 90% of electricity is gas-fired. The Indonesian pipeline contracts end by 2028 and the Malaysian ones may end by 2027 (Wood Mackenzie, July 2025). The figure covers both pipeline suppliers; it is written once, here.
